newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SAS to unveil broad international alliance.
newsitem.headline: SAS to unveil broad international alliance.

text.p: Scandinavian airline SAS said Thursday it would unveil details of an alliance with three other international carriers next month.

It is almost a year since SAS and Germany's Lufthansa joined forces, and the Scandinavian carrier is now embarking on the next stage -- a cooperation with United Airlines, Thai International and Air Canada.
"We will release details in Frankfurt on May 14," SAS spokesman Peter Forssman said.
"The idea is not for a merger of the five airlines but it is based on commercial agreements where bonus programmes, streamlining and seamless service are part of the cooperation."
In February SAS declined to comment on market talks that it was to participate in a new nine-airline global airline, designed to counter the partnership between British Airways and American Airlines.
The new club was to be headed by United and Lufthansa and include Air Canada, SAS, Thai Airways International, Brazil's Varig, Japan's All-Nippon Airways, South African Airways and British Midland.
The alliance between the five carriers will involve over 180,000 employees and almost 1,300 planes.

The biggest player in the team will be United Airlines, which is the largest U.S. carrier and has about 570 planes and 86,000 staff, followed by Lufthansa and Air Canada with about 220 planes and 25,000 staff.
SAS has 161 planes and 25,000 employees, while Thai has 73 planes and 22,000 staff.
